title: Lifecycle Fragility Matrix Workbook
content:
Purpose:
This workbook introduces the ‘Lifecycle Fragility Index’ (LFI), a complementary health-scoring construct intended to surface customers whose usage patterns show fragility or sudden deterioration that traditional steady-state scores miss. It’s designed as an engineering-forward, pragmatic sheet for CS analysts to prototype signals, tune thresholds, and produce deterministic runbook actions for QBR and renewal motion teams.

High level idea:
- Traditional health scores capture absolute levels (engagement, usage, NPS). LFI measures instability: sudden drops, volatility spikes, missing critical events, or loss of high-leverage features.
- Fragility is often a leading indicator of churn when combined with absolute low health. It’s especially useful for large accounts where small changes can cascade into renewal risk.

Key signals (columns to include in sheet):
1) active_users_28d (int) — rolling active users last 28 days
2) act_users_delta_7d_pct (float) — % change last 7d vs previous 7d
3) session_duration_median_7d (mins)
4) key_feature_calls_7d (int) — counts for top-3 revenue-driving features
5) error_rate_7d (pct) — service or integration error rate seen from telemetry
6) support_tickets_14d (int) — tickets filed in last 14 days
7) exec_contact_events_90d (int) — meetings with exec sponsor or AE touchpoints
8) sentiment_change_30d (float) — semantic sentiment trend in CS notes / NPS comments
9) billing_alerts_90d (bool) — failed payments, plan downgrades or invoice disputes
10) volatility_index (float) — composite measure of normalized SD across key metrics (see formula)
11) lifecycle_fragility_index (float) — computed score (0–100), higher = more fragile

Recommended formula (sheet-friendly):
- volatility_index = mean(normalize(sd(active_users_28d, session_duration_median_7d, key_feature_calls_7d))) * 100
- drop_penalty = max(0, -act_users_delta_7d_pct) * 2 + max(0, -sentiment_change_30d) * 1.5 + (support_tickets_14d * 0.5)
- LFI_raw = volatility_index + drop_penalty + (billing_alerts_90d ? 25 : 0) + (error_rate_7d * 10)
- lifecycle_fragility_index = min(100, round(LFI_raw))

Risk tiers (thresholds — tune with cohort):
- Green (LFI <= 12): stable — no proactive outreach except standard cadence
- Watch (13–30): monitor & automated check-ins (CSM touch + email)
- At Risk (31–55): immediate CSM outreach; prioritize enablement and technical triage
- Fragile (56–79): escalate to TAM/AE; propose short-term remediation plan and check infrastructure/usage blockers
- Critical (80+): executive engagement; consider renewal retention offers and fast-track engineering support

Sample worksheet rows (examples to copy/paste into sheet):
- Acme Corp | active_users_28d: 142 | act_users_delta_7d_pct: -28 | session_duration_median_7d: 6 | key_feature_calls_7d: 24 | error_rate_7d: 0.9 | support_tickets_14d: 7 | exec_contact_events_90d: 0 | sentiment_change_30d: -0.4 | billing_alerts_90d: true | volatility_index: 38 | LFI: 77 | Tier: Fragile | Action: Escalate to AE/TAM + 48h health check
- Beta Integrations | active_users_28d: 22 | act_users_delta_7d_pct: -5 | session_duration_median_7d: 18 | key_feature_calls_7d: 2 | error_rate_7d: 0.1 | support_tickets_14d: 0 | exec_contact_events_90d: 1 | sentiment_change_30d: 0.0 | billing_alerts_90d: false | volatility_index: 8 | LFI: 9 | Tier: Green | Action: Standard renewal nurture

Action playbook (by tier):
- Watch: send automated diagnostic email template; attach quick self-serve checklist; set 7-day monitor flag in product; CSM notes a light outreach in calendar.
- At Risk: CSM opens a Technical Triage ticket (link to template), requests runbook logs from infra, schedules 1:1 within 72h. If key_feature_calls drop >50%, trigger product enablement session.
- Fragile: 24–48h response SLA; AE looped for commercial levers; offer prioritized bugfix window or pilot of fallback model; track outcomes on ticket and update LFI weekly.
- Critical: Executive brief with retention options; legal/finance included for billing disputes; immediate resource allocation from SRE or eng to remove blockers.

Detections & alerts to wire into the console: 
- LFI crosses threshold + LFI delta > 15 in 7 days -> page CS Ops and create a JIRA (template JIRA-CS-987).
- Key feature calls drop below 30% of baseline and exec_contact_events_90d == 0 -> Auto-create AE outreach task.
- Billing_alerts_90d true -> Finance watchlist + 48h collection outreach.

Calibration guidance and caveats:
- Baseline normalization: calculate baselines by cohort (ARR bands, seat size, vertical) to avoid small-account noise amplification. Use z-score normalization per cohort before volatility computations.
- Avoid double-counting: LFI complements, not replaces, existing health scores. Use as a multiplier or gating mechanism when deciding escalation.
- Look for confounders: planned maintenance, seasonality (e.g., retail), or known churn events (contract end-of-term) — add manual override reason code.

Data sources & ownership:
- Usage telemetry: prod-telemetry pipeline (owned by eng-telemetry).
- Support tickets: Zendesk (cs-ops owner).
- Billing: Stripe / Finance (finance owner).
- Notes & sentiment: CS notes (NLP pipeline maintained by applied-ml).

Implementation checklist (short-term MVP):
- [ ] Add new columns into CS reporting view (BI team ticket).
- [ ] Implement volatility_index script in dbt (applied-ml owner).
- [ ] Spike: sample cohort calibration (top-50 accounts) and backtest LFI vs. past churn windows.
- [ ] Create automation for Watch tier email + At Risk task creation (CS Ops + Platform).

Monitoring & evaluation metrics (to judge LFI value):
- Precision@K: what fraction of top-K LFI flagged accounts churned or required high-touch remediation in 90 days.
- Time-to-detect: median days between first LFI spike and account escalation vs. baseline manual detection.
- False positive rate by cohort: track to tune thresholds.

Communication templates (short samples):
- Watch automated email subject: "Quick check-in: small usage dip we noticed for {{account}}"; body: friendly check-in + link to self-diagnostic.
- At Risk outreach subject: "Requesting 30 minutes to review recent platform behavior for {{account}}"; body: ask for root-cause info, propose triage times.

Next steps & experiment plan:
1) 6-week pilot on 50 mid-ARR customers; compute LFI weekly; CS team to treat At Risk+Fragile according to playbook.
2) Backtest LFI against rolling 12-month churn events; report lift in early detection.
3) If pilot shows >20% improvement in detection lead-time or >10% increase in actionable escalations, move to productize automation in Console.

Notes to analysts / shortcuts:
- Use sample SQL snippet: SELECT customer_id, avg(active_users_28d) OVER (PARTITION BY cohort ORDER BY date ROWS 13 PRECEDING) as baseline ... (refer to dbt model notes).
- Keep a free-text field `manual_override_reason` when teams flag seasonality or contractual reasons (important for retrospective analysis).

Revision history:
- 2024-09-11: initial concept and signal list (Priya).
- 2024-11-03: added volatility_index and sample thresholds (Diego).
- 2025-02-20: updated calibration guidance and pilot plan after ops sync (Maya).

Appendix: quick copyable runbook snippets
- Technical triage JIRA template title: "LFI Incident - {{account}} - {{date}}"; fields: LFI score, top-3 dropped metrics, recent deploys, CSM notes, SLA.
- Short diagnostic checklist to attach: "Can customer reach API?","Are background jobs failing?","Any payment or license change?","Recent model or config rollouts?"

End of workbook.

(Keep this doc as the working iteration for pilot; once validated move a cleaned playbook to Confluence and wire automations into Console alerting.)
